examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Track orientation, adjacency and handedness separately. A reflection reverses handedness, while an in-plane rotation preserves it. For cube nets identify opposite pairs before checking visible triples. For folds undo the last fold first, reflecting every cut across each fold line. Projections must agree simultaneously in footprint and height.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A rectangular sheet is 24×10 cm. It is folded twice, each time perpendicular to the currently longer side through its midpoint. What is the final perimeter in cm?

**Answer: 32.** First fold gives 12×10. The second halves the still-longer 12, giving 6×10. Perimeter=2(6+10)=32 cm. If the longer side changes, the next fold must follow that new longer side.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
A drawing is representative, not necessarily to scale. Use stated lengths and constraints instead of measuring pixels.

A sketch can look similar while having the wrong handedness. Use a labelled feature to check it.
